method: Source and structure review; syntax counts are inventory aids, not visual quality scores. Code fence detection may include comment examples. No project commands were executed.

records.name: Abblix/Oidc.Server
records.observation: Certification and platform information are separated from the quick start, with tables linking to supporting material.
records.lesson: Use badges as entry points to evidence. Keep certification and licensing distinctions explicit; avoid copying the large badge count.

records.name: ai/size-limit
records.observation: The description explains a concrete performance budget, followed by output imagery, audience-specific setup, configuration, and analysis commands.
records.lesson: Choose installation paths by user task, and demonstrate the actual decision the tool helps make. Hide secondary reporting details rather than the first successful command.

records.name: aimeos/aimeos-typo3
records.observation: The extension combines a product image, several installation routes, and illustrated configuration steps.
records.lesson: A setup screenshot should explain a step people can get wrong. Separate package installation from the surrounding application's setup; do not turn every instruction into an image.

records.name: alichtman/shallow-backup
records.observation: A recorded demo leads into motivation, installation, practical backup recipes, configuration, Git integration, and cautionary material.
records.lesson: Organize usage around complete jobs such as backup and restore. Include material risks where readers encounter the relevant operation, with update and recovery guidance.

records.name: alichtman/stronghold
records.observation: A compact logo/demo introduction states the operating-system scope and explicitly distinguishes tested from untested versions.
records.lesson: Put compatibility limits near the promise. Historical version statements need fresh verification; attractive presentation is not evidence that an old integration still works.

records.name: amitmerchant1990/electron-markdownify
records.observation: The editor uses a short title and purpose, a small inline navigation row, a visible recording, and a commented clone/install/run sequence.
records.lesson: A familiar project header plus one working demo can be enough identity. Explain the shortest runnable path without reproducing the whole website or its sponsorship sections.

records.name: amplication/amplication
records.observation: Theme-specific logo sources sit above separate usage and development paths; component setup and resource links are grouped further down.
records.lesson: Distinguish users from contributors and keep the first-use path short. Use light/dark logo variants only when required; large contributor galleries are optional and belong late.

records.name: AntonioFalcaoJr/EventualShop
records.observation: The architecture project uses extensive diagrams, research explanations, collapsible discussions, technology tables, and environment-specific running instructions.
records.lesson: Long-form explanation can suit an architecture showcase. Keep a route to running the project visible, and move deep theory away from the first-use path when it overwhelms it.

records.name: aregtech/areg-sdk
records.observation: A concrete deployment promise is paired with explanatory visuals, performance sections, alternatives, learning routes, and a project-status section.
records.lesson: Show what changes across deployment modes and identify which route fits which reader. Performance comparisons need workload and measurement context, not decorative speed claims.

records.name: Armync/Arminc-AutoExec
records.observation: The repository's presentation lives in .github/README.md, with an inline menu, configuration screenshots, and distinct update instructions for customized files.
records.lesson: Discover the actual README location before editing. Explain how updates preserve user customization; verify asset paths relative to the document rather than assuming a root README.

records.name: athityakumar/colorls
records.observation: Usage is broken down by flags and illustrated output, followed by install, recommended/custom configuration, update, and removal instructions.
records.lesson: Pair options with the output they change. Treat configuration, update, and removal as part of onboarding when they are necessary; keep oversized novelty badges out of the default style.

records.name: aurumz-rgb/ReviewAid
records.observation: The assistant separates online/local usage, model status, provider configuration, privacy explanations, workflow stages, and screenshots.
records.lesson: AI repositories benefit from precise provider requirements and a clear data flow. Support tables must identify tested conditions; do not turn provider logos into implied endorsements.

records.name: Bonevane/Bridge
records.observation: Problem statements lead into a solution walkthrough, connection/security states, platform screenshots, and separate release/source setup.
records.lesson: Use a state table when exposure or behavior changes with connection mode. Prioritize installing a release for users and building source for developers; copy the reasoning, not the artwork.

records.name: brenocq/implot3d
records.observation: The plotting library supplies an API example, visible demos, integration guidance, an important usage note, and a question-driven FAQ.
records.lesson: Proof should connect to a small code sample. Dynamic roadmap imagery is optional maintenance work; do not add automatically updating graphics to a young repo without a clear need.

records.name: ccostan/Home-AssistantConfig
records.observation: A large personal configuration repository documents its purpose, missing local files, layout, useful starting examples, hardware, and affiliate material.
records.lesson: Disclose intentionally omitted private configuration and point readers to usable examples. Its very dense badge/link inventory is a caution against measuring quality by asset count.

records.name: choojs/choo
records.observation: A small framework combines a distinct authorial voice, one practical example, philosophy, API explanations, an ecosystem, and common questions.
records.lesson: Natural copy comes from specific choices and explanations. Preserve that voice rather than adding generic marketing; do not force a short README when a project's conceptual guide is genuinely useful.

records.name: chroline/well_app
records.observation: The app leads with download/platform availability and quick links, followed by project philosophy, implementation context, and contribution information.
records.lesson: Lead with the route a user needs, and distinguish available platforms from planned ones. A source build is not always the right first action for an app.

records.name: CoffeeIsAllYouNeed/Invisible-Driver
records.observation: The hardware/software project separates play instructions, physical assembly, software setup, directory structure, pipeline, and results.
records.lesson: Separate physical prerequisites from software installation and offer a clearly labelled non-hardware route when it exists. Use photographs/diagrams for steps where text alone is ambiguous.

records.name: create-go-app/cli
records.observation: The CLI presents a package-manager quick start and container alternative, followed by commands, templates, deployment components, and a linked wiki.
records.lesson: Offer one recommended start before alternatives. Group template/component catalogs as reference material rather than making every option compete in the first screen.

records.name: Day8/re-frame
records.observation: The current README is a compact conceptual introduction pointing to documentation, diagnostics, release information, and help.
records.lesson: Check current source rather than assuming a curator's older description is still accurate. A short README can act as a well-labelled gateway to a substantial handbook.

records.name: dbt-labs/dbt-core
records.observation: The current source begins with a major-version/branch warning and separates product explanation, supported environments, starting links, and contribution routes.
records.lesson: An upgrade or branch notice can legitimately outrank branding. Keep version transitions and implementation changes explicit; resolve moved repositories before drawing conclusions.

records.name: dmunish/notecharts
records.observation: A chart gallery supports a short positioning explanation, installation, minimal usage, palette/template examples, export behavior, and attribution.
records.lesson: Visual output is the evidence for a visualization library. Connect a small example to a meaningful image and explain how to save or export the result.

records.name: dmunish/reach
records.observation: Problem and solution sections lead to a process explanation, technology map, visuals, roadmap, and acknowledgements.
records.lesson: An explanatory diagram should show a relationship readers need to understand. Avoid substituting a technology-logo collection for first-use instructions or product evidence.

records.name: doomemacs/doomemacs
records.observation: An official-domain warning precedes installation, documentation links, screenshots, features, prerequisites, roadmap, help, and contribution policy.
records.lesson: Put consequential trust notices where readers will see them. Use the current canonical project name/domain, and preserve actual contributor policies rather than importing generic ones.

records.name: dowjones/react-dropdown-tree-select
records.observation: The component offers a screenshot, multiple demo contexts, install routes, peer requirements, extensive props, styling, accessibility, and performance notes.
records.lesson: Let readers try a working example before scanning a long API. Separate installation from peer requirements; include interaction/accessibility guidance when users integrate a UI component.

records.name: dsplce-co/supabase-plus
records.observation: Task-specific command demonstrations accompany several install options, requirements, completions, and update guidance.
records.lesson: Name the job a command performs and show its result. Use a few focused recordings rather than one long tour, and give a recommended install route before optional package managers.

records.name: dutrevis/spark-resources-metrics-plugin
records.observation: User preparation/install/usage are separated from developer architecture, implementation details, prior art, and next steps; long variants use disclosure blocks.
records.lesson: Use reader roles to divide documentation. Collapsible details are useful for secondary platform/configuration variants, but the default successful route should remain visible.

records.name: EduardaSRBastos/my-essential-toolbox
records.observation: A categorized tool inventory is paired with screenshot evidence, use guidance, performance material, and contribution/license sections.
records.lesson: Group a collection by the jobs it serves. Treat performance screenshots as evidence with conditions, not as universally applicable score badges.

records.name: electrikhq/slate
records.observation: A concise framework-specific promise links to docs and components, followed by screenshots, a short integration sequence, examples, requirements, and security information.
records.lesson: Document the whole first success, including stylesheet import/build/use when required. Keep ecosystem and AI integration claims tied to actual files and instructions.

records.name: emalderson/ThePhish
records.observation: An end-to-end analyst scenario precedes implementation, container/manual setup, configuration, tested integrations, and references.
records.lesson: A narrative task can demonstrate a complex tool better than an abstract feature list. Separate dependencies and provider/configuration assumptions, and keep test claims scoped to actual integrations.

records.name: eylon-44/Buzz-OS
records.observation: The hobby operating system has quick-start requirements/build/run steps, then deeper manuals and capability explanations, with an intentionally playful voice.
records.lesson: Reader-appropriate personality can feel human without adding decoration. Keep jokes subordinate to explicit prerequisites and the first runnable command.

records.name: feberts/python-game-server
records.observation: A small architecture diagram supports a short purpose statement, use cases, a client example, extension guidance, and operational details.
records.lesson: Use one diagram when it removes an explanatory burden. Progress from a complete small example to extension and operation; additional banners are not required.

records.name: FileShot/FileShotZKE
records.observation: Security properties, operating modes, browser compatibility, an API example, and an encryption pipeline are explicit documentation sections.
records.lesson: For security-sensitive tools, explain boundaries and modes before broad assurances. Present claims with evidence and limitations; a nicer README is not a security audit.

records.name: github-changelog-generator/github-changelog-generator
records.observation: The tool explains the reason for its output, then installation/usage, output examples, configuration, migration, alternatives, and FAQ.
records.lesson: Show the generated artifact, not just a command. Preserve migration paths from earlier manual workflows and explain why readers would choose this tool over alternatives.

records.name: gitpoint/git-point
records.observation: The mobile app combines a short promise, screenshots, feature descriptions, feedback, build instructions, contributors, and acknowledgements.
records.lesson: Use actual platform captures to support the promise. Separate consuming an app from contributing to its source; retain credits without letting supporter blocks displace onboarding.

records.name: gofiber/fiber
records.observation: A recognizable framework identity leads to install/migration/quickstart, limitations, many runnable examples, ecosystem catalogs, and development guidance.
records.lesson: A limitation is useful adoption information, not bad marketing. Separate a minimal route from an example catalog, and substantiate benchmark comparisons before repeating them.

records.name: gowebly/gowebly
records.observation: The project offers a direct scaffolding command, package-manager alternatives, a guide/learning path, and a concrete motivation for its chosen stack.
records.lesson: A first command should create a useful result with minimal choices. Explain why the project exists in specific terms, without forcing every repo into a lengthy motivation essay.

records.name: Grigorij-Dudnik/Clean-Coder-AI
records.observation: The linked README returned empty content through both file and contents retrieval.
records.lesson: Do not repeat the collection's trailer/logo claims as current observations. Record the empty response and leave source-specific conclusions unverified rather than inventing them.

records.name: GTruf/Driver-Drowsiness-Detector
records.observation: Dependencies, trial/build paths, operating-system instructions, limitations, and feature-specific screenshots/video snippets are grouped explicitly.
records.lesson: Separate using a prepared build from compiling it. Place limitations next to capabilities and document platform-specific loader/runtime issues instead of implying uniform behavior.

records.name: gui-cs/Terminal.Gui
records.observation: The toolkit combines a short cross-platform statement, a hero recording, a template-driven quick start, a minimal code sample, showcase, and migration/help links.
records.lesson: Show the generated first application, then a small source example. Migration and version guidance belong near installation when multiple major versions are in use.

records.name: GyulyVGC/sniffnet
records.observation: The application provides platform downloads, product screenshots, a user manual, troubleshooting, dependency/rendering fixes, and acknowledgements.
records.lesson: Design downloads around supported platforms and actual artifacts. A user manual and common rendering fixes can be more valuable than more decorative header elements.

records.name: haesleinhuepf/bia-bob
records.observation: Notebook tasks are illustrated individually, with example notebooks, prompt guidance, provider setup, data-submission information, and known issues.
records.lesson: For AI tools, show input and result for distinct tasks. Explain what data reaches which provider; distinguish prerequisites and API keys from an apparent no-setup demo.

records.name: Hexworks/Zircon
records.observation: The library highlights a major-version change, dependency setup, a first window, embedding, terminal use, module/target compatibility, and examples.
records.lesson: Organize first use by the integration surface. State current version and supported targets explicitly rather than leaving readers to infer them from badges.

records.name: hmpl-language/hmpl
records.observation: A tiny templating example leads into DOM use, rationale, features, multiple install paths, official tools, and contribution links.
records.lesson: A concise input/output example can explain a language faster than branding. Compare syntax or behavior concretely; do not expand every capability into a separate marketing card.

records.name: htmlhint/HTMLHint
records.observation: The linter provides a brief tagline/menu, local and global installation, sample output, configuration, and linked documentation.
records.lesson: Distinguish local development dependency setup from global CLI use. Show diagnostic output and the required runtime version, with deeper rules in dedicated docs.

records.name: httpie/httpie
records.observation: A recognizable logo and terminal recording support simple commands, feature explanations, and focused docs/community links.
records.lesson: A few realistic commands can be the strongest visual evidence for a CLI. Keep essential usage visible even if project news or promotional material is present.

records.name: hywax/mafl
records.observation: The homepage tool supplies a cover, themed examples, several deployment routes, services/configuration, languages, and credits.
records.lesson: Show the configuration alongside the visual change it makes. Make one deployment route easy to follow and keep service catalogs and theme galleries secondary.

records.name: IgorAntun/node-chat
records.observation: A short project page shows the interface and describes features, permissions/admin levels, setup, usage, and a live-demo link.
records.lesson: Connect screenshots to real capabilities and permission differences. Treat old externally hosted demos and image links as items to verify, not as permanently valid proof.

records.name: iharsh234/WebApp
records.observation: A screenshot sequence covers landing, filled input, charts, and mobile behavior, with development and issue links.
records.lesson: A small sequence can tell a task story better than unrelated screenshots. Do not inherit unsupported financial performance promises from example prose.

records.name: ivanperez-keera/Yampa
records.observation: The language/library documents installation variants, examples and applications, backends, publications, contribution rules, and versioning/history.
records.lesson: Research-oriented projects need provenance and conceptual context alongside runnable examples. Distinguish cited work, downstream use, and current support; do not turn citations into testimonials.

records.name: JoyHak/MarkdownToBBCode
records.observation: The converter explains the author's actual use case and contains conversion/reference tables, disclosure blocks, and command-line guidance.
records.lesson: Before/after syntax is the proof for a converter. Keep concrete transformations readable and searchable; long conversion matrices belong behind navigation or in reference docs.

records.name: JoyHak/QuickSwitch
records.observation: A real file-dialog problem leads to recorded behaviors, install guidance, detailed settings, limitations, and compilation instructions.
records.lesson: Use a task narrative and feature-specific recordings. Collapse secondary settings to reduce scanning cost, but keep the default operation and platform restrictions visible.

records.name: karan/joe
records.observation: A succinct CLI promise is followed by binary/source installation and concrete overwrite, append, multi-language, and global-file recipes.
records.lesson: Explain the effect of commands on existing files. Offer binary installation first when appropriate, and distinguish append from overwrite where a copied command could lose data.

records.name: kopach/karma-sabarivka-reporter
records.observation: The reporter documents motivation, installation, API, and several configuration examples, with navigation back to an index.
records.lesson: Pair options with exact integration examples. Reserve repeated back-to-top links for genuinely long documents; avoid badge or social-material clutter around small packages.

records.name: L0garithmic/FastColabCopy
records.observation: A compact header/menu and recording support notebook import, usage examples, best practices, and credits.
records.lesson: Show the minimal notebook cell and expected task flow. Performance multipliers need reproducible conditions; do not repeat them just because a curated README states them.

records.name: lobehub/lobe-chat
records.observation: The current project uses language switching, product graphics, task-stage storytelling, marketplace/docs links, and separate self-host/local-development paths.
records.lesson: Translate product lifecycle into user-facing examples when that is the product. Keep self-hosting distinct from a hosted service and avoid copying a large company's promotional density.

records.name: lobehub/sd-webui-lobe-theme
records.observation: The theme project separates extension installation, visual customization examples, environment support, ecosystem, and development.
records.lesson: For appearance tools, use matched theme/feature screenshots as evidence. Include host/environment constraints and a rollback or update path when installation changes another tool.

records.name: ma-shamshiri/Human-Activity-Recognition
records.observation: The academic project uses a dataset/prerequisite/folder map, preprocessing explanation, experiment/results sections, and references, largely with HTML headings.
records.lesson: Research repositories need dataset provenance and reproducible method/result context. Detect HTML headings as well as Markdown; decorative dividers do not add scientific credibility.

records.name: ma-shamshiri/Pacman-Game
records.observation: The project organizes algorithm scenarios with animations, file roles, setup, and credits rather than a generic product feature catalog.
records.lesson: Tie each demonstration to its algorithm or experiment. Explain how to reproduce a scenario, and use only a small number of representative animations in the main document.

records.name: ma-shamshiri/Spam-Detector
records.observation: The classifier explains executable/output/source-file roles, the method, execution steps, and references, with an animated example.
records.lesson: For small school/research projects, a concise file map and real command can carry the README. Do not pad it with SaaS-style sections or fabricated production claims.

records.name: MananTank/radioactive-state
records.observation: Reactive-state examples compare familiar code with the alternative, include recordings, motivations, batching/behavior explanations, and FAQ.
records.lesson: Teach a new API through precise before/after code. Treat speed comparisons as measurements requiring setup and conditions, rather than adopting enthusiastic wording as evidence.

records.name: Martinsos/edlib
records.observation: The library has a minimal call, multiple integration/build approaches, result handling, algorithm/complexity discussion, testing, and publication links.
records.lesson: Separate consuming a library from building it. Link scientific provenance and explain result semantics; installation choices should identify which reader each approach fits.

records.name: mkosir/react-parallax-tilt
records.observation: A focused effect demo links to a live playground, then install, minimal usage, props, device-specific behavior, and development.
records.lesson: Let an interactive component's actual behavior supply the visual interest. Include device requirements and fallbacks; do not add motion to a README simply because its subject uses motion.

records.name: NASA/ogma
records.observation: The runtime-monitor tool separates OS installation, target-specific generation, file formats, template customization, and current limitations.
records.lesson: Document workflows by target and keep limitations next to that target's instructions. Explain generated artifacts and input formats, not just a general capabilities list.

records.name: nhn/tui.editor
records.observation: The editor distinguishes packages, framework wrappers, plugins, visual modes, examples, browser support, and contributor setup.
records.lesson: In multi-package repos, clearly identify what users should install. Separate core package, wrappers, and optional plugins so a polished feature list does not hide the package boundary.

records.name: NSRare/NSGIF
records.observation: The video-to-GIF library uses its own output to demonstrate conversion, then supplies embedding, installation, practical use, and a demo.
records.lesson: Use the tool's real output as the showcase when possible. Keep the example's source and avoid relying on personal cloud-file links for essential repository evidence.

records.name: Owloops/updo
records.observation: A terminal demo precedes installation variants, examples, options, configuration, remote monitoring, and documentation.
records.lesson: Progress from one useful command to advanced recipes. Collapse secondary installation or configuration variants; keep credentials and remote-execution assumptions explicit.

records.name: php-censor/php-censor
records.observation: A dependency table, installation/update links, example project configuration, migrations, test/style commands, and documentation support the server screenshot.
records.lesson: Operational software needs upgrade and migration guidance as well as fresh installation. Keep requirements and example configuration tied to the actual supported version.

records.name: PlexRipper/PlexRipper
records.observation: The current README is primarily an external-site gateway with screenshot/community links and a star request.
records.lesson: An external docs site may justify brevity, but leave enough purpose and first-use guidance in the repo to survive a broken site. Do not infer setup steps from an older listing description.

records.name: PostHog/posthog
records.observation: The page distinguishes hosted use from advanced self-hosting, links to product proof/docs, and explains open-source versus paid components.
records.lesson: Adoption choices should reflect real deployment and licensing boundaries. Separate what readers can run freely from hosted or commercial features without burying that distinction.

records.name: priyavrat-misra/xrays-and-gradcam
records.observation: The study presents introduction/method, model-result images, metric tables, usage, conclusions, and references.
records.lesson: Pair research figures with the data, method, and reproduction route that give them meaning. Never upgrade model metrics or medical claims through visual polish alone.

records.name: Rebilly/redoc
records.observation: The documentation generator highlights major-version migration, a live demo, multiple embedding routes, configuration, hosted comparisons, telemetry, and releases.
records.lesson: A migration notice and embedding decision tree can prevent wrong installs. Explain generated output and telemetry accurately; keep hosted versus open-source features distinct.

records.name: refinedev/refine
records.observation: A browser try-out and scaffolding command support a precise framework position, use cases, learning links, and contribution paths.
records.lesson: Reduce the cost of evaluating the product with a working browser example when one exists. Explain the framework's actual role rather than adding generic productivity claims.

records.name: release-it/release-it
records.observation: The release tool documents interactive/CI usage, configuration, existing releases, hooks, dry runs, troubleshooting, and plugins.
records.lesson: Side-effecting tools need a safe preview route and a clear explanation of what a command changes. Keep configuration examples and runtime support easy to find.

records.name: rstacruz/hicat
records.observation: The tiny CLI explains behavior with direct commands, a terminal recording, installation, and a few tips.
records.lesson: Small useful tools can have short useful READMEs. Let an actual command/result carry the document instead of adding mandatory banners, roadmaps, or feature grids.

records.name: ryanoasis/nerd-fonts
records.observation: The font collection combines notices, a quick route, a download catalog, variants, many install paths, patching examples, and troubleshooting.
records.lesson: Large asset collections need a selection/download taxonomy before technical details. Explain unstable paths and variant naming, and avoid cloning a large repo when a small release asset suffices.

records.name: sebyddd/SDVersion
records.observation: The device library uses platform-specific usage and supported-model/API lists after recommended and alternative installation paths.
records.lesson: Support should be a structured, version-sensitive reference. Separate platform requirements from examples and do not describe a long device list as a guarantee for untested future hardware.

records.name: serpro69/kotlin-faker
records.observation: The data generator separates prerequisites, Gradle/Maven installation, version alignment, usage, extensions, and release/contribution tasks.
records.lesson: Provide the ecosystem's native install idioms and identify version coordination when relevant. Contributor release instructions should not interrupt a user's first sample.

records.name: shama/gaze
records.observation: The library moves quickly from a specific file-watching promise to examples, alternate API, errors, patterns, and reference material.
records.lesson: Show error behavior and event semantics alongside happy-path code. Keep runtime compatibility fresh; an old badge or range is not a current environment test.

records.name: shivrajsinhzala/transit-timetables
records.observation: The data-backed site documents refresh operations, hosting, indexing choices, branding, data logic, and attribution with little decorative imagery.
records.lesson: A repository's real job may be maintaining a data pipeline rather than installing an app. Document provenance, refresh cadence, and operational effects instead of imposing product-launch sections.

records.name: shriyanyamali/JurisMercatus
records.observation: The searchable database explains purpose, feature evidence, infrastructure, manual/container setup, data sources, and attribution.
records.lesson: Explain where data comes from and what search does. Separate infrastructure/source repositories when that helps contributors, and keep legal/data attribution attached to the demo.

records.name: sidneycadot/oeis
records.observation: A simple diagram/map explains remote, mirror, and local analysis sources and the scripts that connect them.
records.lesson: A source/data-flow map is useful when file names alone hide the workflow. Use a small explanatory diagram, not a technology collage or an exhaustive directory dump.

records.name: sindresorhus/pageres
records.observation: The screenshot tool uses a real output illustration, a minimal API call, an option reference, and links to downstream uses.
records.lesson: Demonstrate the output at the sizes readers care about. Keep API examples complete and move optional browser flags/advanced options behind the primary task.

records.name: skydio/revup
records.observation: A step-by-step tutorial uses scenario recordings to explain independent/dependent review branches, edits, upstream updates, and configuration.
records.lesson: For workflow tools, a story of an actual change is stronger than abstract feature cards. Explain compatibility and the state a command changes before showcasing advanced options.

records.name: sourcerer-io/sourcerer-app
records.observation: The profile tool combines a visual result, private-repository explanation, permission questions, configuration, and local build/run guidance.
records.lesson: Explain permission and privacy requirements before asking readers to connect private source. Distinguish profile-presentation tools from what belongs in a product README.

records.name: sr6033/lterm
records.observation: The tutorial emulator presents supported commands, extension candidates, and a concrete contribution example.
records.lesson: Tell readers what is implemented versus planned. Describe the smallest contribution pathway; large ASCII branding is an optional historical style, not a default to reproduce.

records.name: Stack-in-a-box/triumphmayflowerclub.com
records.observation: A contributor-oriented site repo documents links, versions, local prerequisites, development, deployment, and content/technical roadmap details.
records.lesson: Match depth to the actual maintainer audience. A website repository may need content-editing instructions and deployment context more than an API or package install section.

records.name: stevenfoncken/multitool-for-spotify-php
records.observation: The tool separates requirements, installation, environment/API setup, concrete tasks, development, and questions/credits.
records.lesson: An external API dependency belongs in setup, including what configuration is required. Use task names and expected artifacts; do not include real secrets in copied examples.

records.name: sultan99/react-on-lambda
records.observation: The library explains the syntax tradeoff using code, example images, benchmarks, editor configuration, and API links.
records.lesson: A rationale is most useful when it compares concrete authoring patterns. Keep alternatives and measured performance specific; avoid general claims that one style is universally better.

records.name: sulu/sulu
records.observation: A product image and short CMS overview point to installation/docs, community, contribution, requirements, and license.
records.lesson: An established documentation site allows a compact repository landing page. Keep purpose and requirements local enough that readers can decide whether following the docs is worthwhile.

records.name: supunlakmal/thismypc
records.observation: The multi-component app presents product flows, folder/component roles, per-component setup, API reference, and licensing.
records.lesson: A component map should answer where contributors work and how parts start together. Keep the user's first path separate from a long internal development guide.

records.name: teles/array-mixer
records.observation: Visual examples and code recipes explain array interleaving, supported options, migration, TypeScript support, and edge cases.
records.lesson: Use small before/after data and task-specific examples for an algorithmic utility. Include exhaustion/limit behavior and API migration instead of relying on an abstract feature list.

records.name: thelounge/thelounge
records.observation: The self-hosted client combines a small header/nav, screenshot, features, and clearly separated stable/source/development routes.
records.lesson: Users should not have to guess whether a command installs a release or starts an unbuilt checkout. A concise screenshot and three clear routes can replace a long marketing page.

records.name: themerdev/themer
records.observation: A visual explanation connects input colors to generated themes/wallpapers, with CLI/API workflows, output catalogs, and prior art.
records.lesson: Show the transformation from input to generated artifacts. Catalog output targets and integration examples without making all targets compete in the opening.

records.name: treeverse/dvc
records.observation: The source uses reStructuredText substitutions and sections for product positioning, docs/navigation, installation, usage/support, and community.
records.lesson: Read the actual document format instead of treating missing Markdown headings/images as missing content. Preserve the project's format unless a conversion is requested.

records.name: vhesener/Closures
records.observation: Small closure-handler code examples show the abstraction immediately, followed by a playground, references, several install options, and conceptual background.
records.lesson: A minimal idiomatic code sample can explain a library better than a slogan. Put richer exploration in a playground and use background material to clarify tradeoffs.

records.name: voltagent/voltagent
records.observation: The agent framework has a quick scaffold, first workflow, examples, observability screens, deployment, guardrails/evaluation material, and language links.
records.lesson: An agent repo needs a runnable first task and actual tool/configuration requirements. Feature screenshots should correspond to working components rather than a broad AI-platform promise.

records.name: xnbox/DeepfakeHTTP
records.observation: Concrete HTTP request/response examples support use cases, setup, detailed options, and example behavior; much structure uses HTML.
records.lesson: For a protocol/mock server, the request and response are the showcase. Detect HTML structure and explain executable configuration rather than replacing it with decorative diagrams.

records.name: yeaight7/awesome-ai-devtools
records.observation: The catalog separates reviewed and draft entries, groups by user intent and technical category, and includes a comparison matrix and contribution rules.
records.lesson: Collections need transparent review state and a consistent selection vocabulary. Do not turn a directory into an unfiltered keyword list or confuse a listing with a verified integration.

records.name: yvann-ba/ft_transcendence
records.observation: The project presents gameplay imagery, prerequisites, environment configuration, OS-specific container startup, access instructions, and a system explanation.
records.lesson: A first-success guide should finish at an observable URL/action. Distinguish example environment values from secrets and explain OS-specific commands where they differ.

records.name: zenml-io/zenml
records.observation: The ML platform provides a quick install/init/login route, architecture/demo links, ecosystem resources, FAQs, and editor integrations.
records.lesson: Keep client versus server installation choices explicit. Tie time-to-start promises to actual prerequisites; state which integrations are implemented rather than inferring them from the audience.

records.name: Amazing GitHub Template
records.observation: The template exposes setup paths, variables, community files, and contribution conventions.
records.lesson: Treat templates as optional scaffolding. Replace placeholders and omit irrelevant sections; copying an entire community-file hierarchy does not establish a real support or security process.

records.name: Github Licenses Stats
records.observation: The card generator shows Markdown/HTML embedding, query parameters, themes, and a live endpoint.
records.lesson: A stats widget is optional presentation infrastructure with an external dependency. Do not confuse license statistics with the target repository's actual legal terms.

records.name: GitHub PR Stats
records.observation: The widget supplies distinct timeline/aggregate modes, theme examples, configuration, and deployment instructions.
records.lesson: Record what a visual statistic measures and where it comes from. Contribution statistics are appropriate to profiles/portfolios, not proof of a product's usability.

records.name: GitHub Stats Extended
records.observation: The stats project distinguishes card types and gives a concrete migration route from an earlier service.
records.lesson: External badge/card services can change ownership or availability. Verify the current endpoint and keep essential repo information usable when a widget fails.

records.name: GPRM
records.observation: The profile generator groups social, stack, visitor, trophy, donation, and statistics elements into configurable features.
records.lesson: Separate profile design from project documentation. Do not import a profile's social badges, trophies, or visitor counters into every product README.

records.name: Hall-of-fame
records.observation: The contributor widget explains its selection categories, live examples, embedding, and FAQ.
records.lesson: Recognize actual contributors with consent-appropriate public data and a real source. Keep galleries below onboarding; refreshing an external widget introduces maintenance and availability costs.

records.name: README best practices
records.observation: The tool demonstrates replacing an empty README with a template and then filling it with project-specific content.
records.lesson: A template is a starting point, not evidence. Never overwrite an existing README blindly; extract project facts and remove irrelevant boilerplate before saving.

records.name: readme-md-generator
records.observation: The generator reads project metadata to propose defaults and shows the interactive generation flow.
records.lesson: Derive name, license, commands, and links from inspected files. Confirm uncertain facts instead of inventing them; metadata-derived text still needs editorial judgment.

records.name: README Typing SVG
records.observation: The animated-text service supplies an embeddable example, a demo configurator, sizing/options, and self-hosting guidance.
records.lesson: Do not put essential meaning only in animated text. Default to static selectable copy; use decorative typing effects only when explicitly useful, with size and dependency costs considered.

records.name: READMINE
records.observation: The suggested structure covers purpose, installation, first use, deeper usage, limitations, help, contributions, and acknowledgements.
records.lesson: Distinguish an installation step from a useful first task. Use limitations and help sections when there is real content; do not publish unfilled suggested sections.

records.name: Standard Readme
records.observation: The specification emphasizes consistent install/usage/navigation conventions and links examples and generation tools.
records.lesson: Familiar headings and predictable first-use information are valuable defaults. A compliance badge should reflect real compliance, not merely borrowing the badge image.

records.name: Telegram Card
records.observation: The social card widget explains source types, themes, embedding, live samples, deployment, and local development.
records.lesson: An external social card is relevant only when that channel helps users. Keep its numbers and source scope clear; do not let social presence replace product evidence.

records.name: user-statistician
records.observation: The statistics Action pairs workflows with resulting image samples, detailed inputs, versioning, permissions, branch concerns, and examples.
records.lesson: A generated visual needs a documented source and refresh path. Use minimum required workflow permissions and a deliberate version policy; do not add background automation solely for decoration.

records.name: Zalando's README Template
records.observation: The checklist explicitly encourages selecting only relevant sections and covers purpose, concepts, requirements, contribution, contact, and license.
records.lesson: Use a coverage checklist, not a fixed page formula. Section omission is a valid editorial decision when it improves the actual reader's path.

records.name: Gifski
records.observation: The app provides download/platform guidance, screenshots, practical export tips, source-build instructions, and GIF-size FAQs.
records.lesson: Choose capture/export tools for the available OS and optimize motion length, dimensions, and frame rate. Do not make an app's source-build path the default user download.

records.name: ScreenToGif
records.observation: The recording app separates runtime requirements, download/store routes, and visual feature demonstrations.
records.lesson: Check host/runtime prerequisites before recommending a recorder. Use actual capture/edit/export behavior and avoid assuming the same application runs on every OS.

records.name: terminalizer
records.observation: The terminal recorder documents record/play/render/share flows, compression, timing, themes, and frame options.
records.lesson: Keep editable recording configuration alongside the result. Prefer a real terminal capture without fake browser/IDE chrome and optimize duration and file size.

records.name: ttystudio
records.observation: The recorder includes an actual recording sequence, expected compilation messages, trimming, timing, font selection, and output options.
records.lesson: A recorded command and its source make a demo maintainable. Trim dead time and keep a readable static fallback rather than relying on animation alone.

records.name: vhs
records.observation: The recorder treats demonstrations as source-controlled tape files, links output to its source, and documents commands and settings.
records.lesson: Prefer reproducible demos when practical. Commit a small recording source with the relevant example and regenerate it when behavior changes; do not run installers merely to decorate a README.

records.name: Neovim architecture
records.observation: The architecture README is now a short relocation notice pointing to developer documentation.
records.lesson: A moved-document stub should send readers to its canonical replacement. Keep links current and do not repeat the collection's old architecture description as if the old file still contains it.

records.name: Redis architecture
records.observation: The current README explicitly routes new users, source builders, and contributors, then covers use cases, setup variants, builds, and troubleshooting.
records.lesson: Use reader-path navigation and make the recommended route clear. Current source can differ from a collection's older source-map description, so inspect before generalizing.

records.name: Understand Anything
records.observation: A concise native header and ordinary badges lead to a real product visual, feature explanations, quick start, detailed host routes, and a compatibility matrix.
records.lesson: Use familiar repository conventions and prove capability before adding decoration. Learn the sequence and clarity, not a large badge count, borrowed brand assets, or unsupported host claims.
